producer_report.summary: Added a code-health check that runs after every landing. It measures each tracked Rust file under a src/ directory with syn: production lines (test modules excluded) and longest function. It counts landings in the last 7 days from git and failure/rejection/plan-stop citations from Records. For each file over a limit (more than 2000 lines, a function over 200 lines, or more than 1500 lines with 5 or more landings in a week) it queues one "Structural pass: <path>" request through Athena::queue with the measured numbers, unless one is open. A new typed record, athena.code-health-baseline/1 (AnyRecord::CodeHealthBaseline, stored under records/code-health/<month>/<id>.json, loaded as Records.code_health_baselines), anchors the cadence. The first check writes the baseline and queues no review. Once 10 landings stand beyond the latest baseline, it queues a self-contained "Priority: high" design review and writes a new baseline. A landing is a first-parent commit with both Athena-Job and Athena-Verified-Content trailers, because records-only commits carry only Athena-Job. The hook runs in Athena::land_pr via a new after_merge (resync, then Pages watch, then check) and in note_finished for Landed outcomes only, before the nested-run return. Errors are shown as warnings only. athena status shows an aligned table plus the limits and suite time (read from the latest recorded "test" check, otherwise "unknown"). CHANGELOG.md has an entry, docs/decisions.md has D132, and docs/records.md lists the new record directory. The full suite was run once after the final code changes except two test fixes; the last two failing test files were rerun and pass.

checks_run.note: Found two existing tests that assumed the landing commit is the branch tip (lifecycle, cutover_fixture) and a third earlier (binary, found by the first run). I fixed all three and reran each file: binary 15 pass, lifecycle 66 pass, cutover_fixture 4 pass. Everything else passed in the full run. I did not rerun the whole suite after these three test edits.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a code_health test with fixture source files and landing records asserts per-file production line count (excluding #[cfg(test)] modules), longest function length, landings in the last 7 days, and failure/rejection citations.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test -p athena-core code_health: measuring_excludes_cfg_test_modules_and_finds_the_longest_function, code_health_counts_lines_functions_weekly_landings_and_citations (asserts lines 26, longest fn 22, weekly 3, records-only and 30-day-old commits not counted) and citations_count_rejected_failed_and_plan_stopped_jobs_that_name_the_file (asserts 2) pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: tests show each threshold breach (file over 2000 lines, function over 200 lines, over 1500 lines with 5 or more landings in a week) is reported, and a file under the thresholds is not flagged.
criteria_check.evidence: breach_reports_each_threshold_and_spares_a_file_under_them (2001/201/1501+5 flagged; 2000, 200, 1501+4, 1500+9 not) and structural_pass_for_a_long_function_and_a_busy_file (real fixture with 202-line function and 5 weekly landings) pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: on a breach exactly one structural-pass request is queued for that file, citing the measured numbers; a second run, or an open structural-pass request for the file, queues none.
criteria_check.evidence: structural_pass_queues_one_request_citing_the_numbers_and_none_on_a_rerun and structural_pass_queues_nothing_for_a_file_with_an_open_request pass; the first asserts the text contains '2001 production lines', the landings count and citations.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a baseline record (new AnyRecord variant in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, with a schema round-trip test) is written, and a test reloads Records from git into a fresh state directory and shows the baseline survives. The first landing sets the baseline and fires no review.
criteria_check.evidence: a_code_health_baseline_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips (athena-data) and the_first_landing_sets_the_baseline_and_queues_no_review (writes baseline, reloads via athena_over with a fresh StateDir, finds it, no second baseline and no review) pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the design-review request is queued through Athena::queue at high priority on the 10th landing after the baseline, and not on the 9th.
criteria_check.evidence: design_review_cadence_queues_on_the_tenth_landing_after_the_baseline_not_the_ninth: no review after 9, review after 10 with JobRecords::priority() == High, no repeat; passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the queued design-review text names what to review (code-health table, files most changed and most broken since the last review, open structural-pass requests, recent rejections and planning stops) and what to produce (a short design note with proposed changes, as a design-only job).
criteria_check.evidence: design_review_text_names_what_to_review_and_what_to_produce asserts each phrase, the table header, the changed-file count, the open structural pass and the rejected job id; passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: tests show the check runs after a landing in both Athena::land_pr (after resync_onto_merge and the Pages watch) and note_finished in steward.rs, and each test fails without its hook. Tests set the disk-guard minimum to 0.
criteria_check.evidence: gh::after_merge_tests::after_a_merge_the_branch_is_resynced_then_pages_watched_then_code_health_checked (shared log shows resync line, then Pages lookup, then code health line; request queued after the merged commit) and a_pull_request_that_did_not_land_is_not_checked; steward::tests::note_finished_checks_code_health_after_a_landing_and_only_then (Landed queues, Rejected/Failed do not, nested Landed does); cli code_health_hooks tests via real ask/go. Each hook removal leaves no queued request, so these fail. Unit fixture and test_config set min_free_gb = 0. Limitation: Athena::land_pr itself calls after_merge but is not run end to end in a test.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the rendered athena status output contains the code-health table with each file's lines, longest function, weekly landings, citations, thresholds, whether over, and test suite run time, with aligned headers.
criteria_check.evidence: display::tests::status_renders_code_health_as_an_aligned_table_with_limits_and_suite_time and cli test status_shows_the_code_health_table_with_the_oversized_file_marked (real Athena::status through display::status) check header columns line up with cells, limits line and 'test suite run time'; pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked: all three exit 0.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran fmt --check and clippy (both exit 0) after the last edits; the full test run had the three failing test files fixed and rerun individually, but the whole suite was not rerun afterward.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and docs/decisions.md records the thresholds, the buy-versus-build call on measuring function length (syn), the baseline record, and the 10-landing cadence.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Added entry; docs/decisions.md D132 states thresholds 2000/200/1500+5 per week, the syn buy-versus-build call, the baseline record, the landing definition and the 10-landing cadence.

open_issues: Cargo.toml (root) was edited to add syn and proc-macro2 to [workspace.dependencies]; it is not in the brief's deliverable list but athena-core needs workspace dependencies, as the plan noted.

Departure: I extracted the post-merge steps of Athena::land_pr into a new pub(crate) after_merge so the order resync, Pages watch, code health can be tested; land_pr calls it, but land_pr itself has no end-to-end test.

Three existing tests were edited because the hook now commits a baseline after a landing: binary.rs (nested-run test looks at the last 3 commits), lifecycle.rs (uses the finished landing commit instead of HEAD), cutover_fixture.rs (the parent of C0 is the baseline commit above the old-way landing).
Suite time is read from the latest verification's check named 'test'; if no job has recorded one, status shows 'unknown'.

On the first run in a repository whose files are already over a limit, one structural-pass request is queued per file (intended; deduplicated afterwards). The real repository may produce several at its next landing.
docs/records.md was edited to list the new records/code-health directory.
mistakes: My first test fixtures used outcome records with a made-up Athena-Record trailer and a Landed outcome; the gate refused them. Fixed by closing jobs with an Athena-Job trailer and non-landed states.
I first used identical timestamps for consecutive baselines, which made 'latest' ambiguous in tests; the tests now advance the time.
I did not rerun the whole suite after the last three test edits (binary, lifecycle, cutover_fixture); I reran those files only, because of the USD budget.
learnings: Records commits (queue, readings) carry an Athena-Job trailer; only landing commits also carry Athena-Verified-Content, so that pair is the way to tell a landing from a records commit.
Records are read with Records::load from a git commit; a baseline in git survives a fresh StateDir because StateDir holds no records.

Any hook that commits records after a landing in go() or land_pr breaks tests that assume the landing is the branch tip (binary nested tests, lifecycle a_request_lands_a_traceable_commit, cutover_fixture c0 parent).
syn 3.0.7 is also in Cargo.lock (another crate); I used syn 2.0.119 as planned.
The producer's Bash policy blocks head, tail and wc, so use Read and Grep for inspecting output files.
desires: A way to run Athena::land_pr end to end in a test without a hand-built verified job, remote and gh fake.
A shared test helper for hand-made landing commits with the Athena trailers.
